Rashi on Shabbat 155b:10:1.english: Because [water is] commonly found in a marsh - But food is not commonly found for them.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:11:1.english: That its sustenance is scarce - For no person has pity on it to give it much sustenance.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:11:2.hebrew: כמה תשהה במעיו - דהכלב שאכל בשר מת, ומת הכלב בבית תוך ג' ימים, מטמא באהל. אבל בחייו לא מטמא, דטומאה בלועה בבעלי חיים לא מיטמא, כדאמר בבהמה המקשה (חולין דף עא:):
Rashi on Shabbat 155b:11:2.english: How long does [its food] remain in its intestines - [Meaning] that if a dog ate flesh of a corpse, and the dog died in a house within three days, it imparts ritual impurity in a tent. However, during its lifetime it does not impart ritual impurity, because swallowed impurity in living creatures does not impart ritual impurity, as it states in [chapter] Behemah HaMakshah (Chullin 71b).

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:12:1.english: Learn from it - Since [the Gemara] says that the Holy One, Blessed be He, was concerned about its sustenance.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:12:2.hebrew: משח אודניה - מעט, כמות אוזנו. וחוטרא בתריה — יכהו במקל מיד, שלא יהא מרגילו אצלו:
Rashi on Shabbat 155b:12:2.english: The measure of its ear - A small amount, like the size of its ear. And "a staff after it" — he should strike it with a stick immediately, so that he does not accustom it [to stay] with him.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:12:3.english: But in a town, [one should] not - give it anything if it is not his.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:12:4.english: Because [it] will come to be drawn - after him, and they will suffer loss.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:12:5.hebrew: לית דעתיר מחזירא - שכל מאכל ראוי לו ומוצא לאכול, ואף מאכילין לו הרבה:
Rashi on Shabbat 155b:12:5.english: There is none richer than a pig - For every food is fit for it and it finds [food] to eat, and they even feed it a great deal.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:13:1.english: In accordance with Rav Yehuda - For hamra'a [is placing food] into a place from which [the animal] cannot return [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:13:2.english: Forces its mouth open - [He] puts a hook into its mouth so that it cannot close its mouth.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:13:3.english: And feeds it vetch and water simultaneously - And the water causes the vetch to be swallowed into its throat against its will.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:13:4.hebrew: מאכילה מעומד - נותן לתוך פיה, וכל זמן שאינו מרביצה אינו יכול לתחוב כל כך, ויכול להחזירה:
Rashi on Shabbat 155b:13:4.english: Feeds it [while] standing - He puts [food] into its mouth, and as long as he does not lay it down, he cannot stuff [it in] so much, and [the animal] can expel it.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:14:1.hebrew: מתניתין מני - דקתני נותן מים לתוך המורסן, דנתינת מים לא זהו גיבולו:
Rashi on Shabbat 155b:14:1.english: Whose [opinion] is the Mishnah - In that it teaches [that] one may put water into the bran, for putting in water is not its kneading.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:15:1.hebrew: אפי' ר' יוסי מודה - דזהו גיבולו:
Rashi on Shabbat 155b:15:1.english: Even Rabbi Yosei concedes - For this is its kneading.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:16:1.hebrew: קלי - קמח של תבואה שנתייבשה כשהן קליות בתנור, ואותו קמח לעולם מתוק, והוא קמחא דאבשונא. ועושין ממנו שתיתא, משמן ומים ומלח שמערבין בו:
Rashi on Shabbat 155b:16:1.english: Kali - Flour of grain that was dried as parched ears in an oven; and that flour is always sweet, and it is kamcha de'avshuna [flour of dried unripe grain]. And they make shetita [a gruel] from it, from oil, water, and salt that they mix into it.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:1:1.hebrew: את הדלועין - התלושין, ולא אמרינן מוקצין הן לבהמה, דמאכל אדם הן:
Rashi on Shabbat 155b:1:1.english: The pumpkins - [Those] that are detached [from the ground], and we do not say [that] they are muktzeh for an animal because they are human food.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:1:3.hebrew: א"נ - כלבים דקאמר, בגורייתא זוטרי, דכל נבלה קשה להן:
Rashi on Shabbat 155b:1:3.english: Alternatively - the dogs that it mentions [are] young puppies, for any carcass is hard for them.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:2:1.hebrew: ומערבין - התבן והאספסתא יחד, והבהמה אוכלת התבן בשביל האספסתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 155b:2:1.english: And mix - the straw and the alfalfa together, and the animal eats the straw on account of the alfalfa.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:2:2.hebrew: תבן בתיבנא סריא - דלא חזיא, והשתא משוי לה אוכלא. והאי סריא לאו סריא לגמרי, דההיא לטינא קיימא ואסורה לטלטל:
Rashi on Shabbat 155b:2:2.english: Straw [refers] to rotten straw - Which was not fit [for consumption], and now he renders it food. And this "rotten" [straw] is not completely rotten, for that [completely rotten straw] is intended for clay and is forbidden to move [on Shabbat].

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:3:1.hebrew: אין אובסין - מאכילין אותו הרבה על כרחו ותוחבין לו בגרונו. ובגמרא מפרש לשון אובסין: עושין לה כמין אבוס בתוך מעיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 155b:3:1.english: One may not forcibly overfeed - [This means] feeding it a great deal against its will and stuffing [food] into its throat. And in the Gemara, it explains the term ovsin: they make for it a sort of manger inside its belly.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:3:2.hebrew: ולא דורסין - שדורס לה בתוך גרונה את השעורין, ומיהו לא הוי כל כך כמו אובסין:
Rashi on Shabbat 155b:3:2.english: And one may not force-feed - [This means] that he presses the barley into its throat; however, it is not as much as forcibly overfeeding.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:3:3.english: However, one may place food into its mouth - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:3:4.english: One may not feed [in the manner of hamra'a] - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:3:5.english: [One may] feed [chickens by putting food into their mouths] - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:3:6.hebrew: אין נותנין מים לפני דבורים - מפרש טעמא בגמרא, אי משום דאין מזונותיהן עליו, שיוצאין ואוכלין בשדה, אי משום דמיא באגמא שכיח להו:
Rashi on Shabbat 155b:3:6.english: One may not place water before bees - [It] explains the reason in the Gemara: whether because their sustenance is not [incumbent] upon him, since they go out and eat in the field, or because water is readily available to them in the marsh.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:3:7.hebrew: הרדיסאות - על שם מקומן, וניזונין בתוך הבית:
Rashi on Shabbat 155b:3:7.english: Hardisian - [Named] after their place, and they are fed inside the house.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:4:1.english: In that manner - That one feeds it so much that its stomach widens like a trough.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:4:2.hebrew: אטענה כורא - על גבה למזונות לדרך, לבד שאר משאות:
Rashi on Shabbat 155b:4:2.english: Loaded it [with] a kor - On its back for provisions for the road, aside from other loads.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:5:1.english: Into a place from which it cannot return [the food] - [Meaning] that he thrusts it into [the animal] beyond the gullet.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:5:2.english: With a vessel - With a ladle.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:6:1.english: That one feeds by hand - One thrusts it into its mouth.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:6:2.hebrew: אלא יוני שובך וכו' - בתמיה, ואמאי לא? מאי טרחא איכא:
Rashi on Shabbat 155b:6:2.english: Rather, doves of a dovecote, etc. - [This is asked] in astonishment: and why not? What exertion is there?

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:7:1.hebrew: אלא לאו כו' - ומדמהלקטין דמתניתין למקום שאינה יכולה להחזיר נמי שרי, שמע מינה מלעיטין דעגלים וגמלים למקום שאינה יכולה להחזיר ושרי, אלא דגבי בהמה קרי ליה הלעטה וגבי עופות קרי ליה הילקוט. ועל כרחך, "אין מאמירין" דקאסר בכלי הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 155b:7:1.english: Rather, is it not, etc. - And since mehalketin of the Mishnah [refers to] a place from which [the bird] cannot return [the food] and [is] nonetheless permitted, learn from this that mal'itin of calves and camels [is also] into a place from which [the animal] cannot return [the food], and it is permitted, except that regarding an animal [the Mishnah] calls it hal'atah, and regarding birds it calls it hilkut. And perforce, "we do not force-feed" [ein ma'amirin] that it prohibits is [done] with a vessel.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:8:1.english: Actually, mehalketin is where one feeds it by hand - and [into] a place from which it can return [the food].

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:8:2.english: Their sustenance is not [incumbent] upon you - For [food] is readily available to them in the field.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:8:3.english: A pig — its sustenance is not upon you - For a Jew who raises pigs is cursed.

Rashi on Shabbat 155b:9:1.english: [The Mishnah] is also precise - That even throwing [it] before them is also not [permitted].

Tosafot on Shabbat 155b:15:1.hebrew: אלא קמח דבר גיבול הוא - פירשתי לעיל בפ"ק (שבת דף יח. ושם):
Tosafot on Shabbat 155b:15:1.english: Only [in the case of] flour, which can be kneaded - I explained [this] earlier in the first chapter (Shabbat 18a, and there).

Tosafot on Shabbat 155b:3:1.hebrew: אין אובסין את הגמל וכו' - והא דאמרינן בעירובין פרק עושין פסין (עירובין דף כ: ושם): "גמל שראשו ורובו מבפנים, אובסין אותו מבפנים" — הך אביסה לאו היינו אביסה ממש, דהא אמרינן הכא "אין אובסין כו'", וההיא אביסה היינו הלעטה; וכן פירש רבינו שמואל:
Tosafot on Shabbat 155b:3:1.english: "One may not forcibly overfeed a camel, etc." - And [as for] that which we say in Eruvin, in the chapter [entitled] Osin Passin (Eruvin 20b and there): "A camel whose head and most of its body are inside, one may feed [ovsin] it inside" — that avisah [lit., forcible overfeeding] is not literal avisah, for we say here, "One may not forcibly overfeed [ovsin], etc."; rather, that avisah means placing food into its mouth [hala'atah]. And so explained Rabbeinu Shmuel.
